Plot total, bioavailable, and relative proportion of bioavailable fractions for both Zn and Cu

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Colors by response variable
#-------------------------------------------------
response_colors <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"                              = "slategray",
  "Bioavailable Zn (nmol/g wet weight)"        = "darkslategray3",
  "Proportion of Bioavailable Zn" = "turquoise",
  "Total Cu (nM)"                              = "chocolate4",
  "Bioavailable Cu (nmol/g wet weight)"        = "peru",
  "Proportion of Bioavailable Cu" = "chocolate1"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Map variable names -> response labels
#-------------------------------------------------
response_lookup <- c(
  "log_Zn_nM"         = "Total Zn (nM)",
  "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g" = "Bioavailable Zn (nmol/g wet weight)",
  "log_rel_prop_Zn"   = "Proportion of Bioavailable Zn",
  "log_Cu_nM"         = "Total Cu (nM)",
  "log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g" = "Bioavailable Cu (nmol/g wet weight)",
  "log_rel_prop_Cu"   = "Proportion of Bioavailable Cu"
)

vars_trace <- names(response_lookup)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Long data for plotting (Zn vars from zn_dat, Cu vars from cu_dat)
#-------------------------------------------------

# Keep only what's needed from each dataset
zn_keep <- c("Sample_ID", "Typology", "log_Zn_nM", "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g", "log_rel_prop_Zn")
cu_keep <- c("Sample_ID", "Typology", "log_Cu_nM", "log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g", "log_rel_prop_Cu")

# Full-join so we get one row per Typology/sample combination.
# If your data are one-row-per-sample, and Typology is a sample attribute,
# you almost certainly also need Sample_ID here. See note below.
dat_wide_trace <- full_join(
  zn_dat %>% dplyr::select(any_of(zn_keep)),
  cu_dat %>% dplyr::select(any_of(cu_keep)),
  by = c("Sample_ID", "Typology")
)

# Pivot long exactly like before
dat_long_trace <- dat_wide_trace %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, any_of(vars_trace)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = names(response_colors))
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. One faceted trace element panel (x = Typology)
#-------------------------------------------------
bioavail_panel <- ggplot(dat_long_trace, aes(
  x     = Typology,
  y     = Value,
  color = Response
)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~ Response, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Trace Elements by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )

bioavail_panel

# Save as square
ggsave(
  filename = file.path("Trace_elements_panel_square.png"),
  plot     = bioavail_panel,
  width    = 8.5,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)

# Save as rectangle
ggsave(
  filename = file.path("Trace_elements_panel_long.png"),
  plot     = bioavail_panel,
  width    = 14,
  height   = 8,
  dpi      = 300
)
```
